output.brief:
Don't roll back gateway 5.8. The latency jump comes from the 2 Nov compaction tuning change on storage nodes (FC-7710), not from the gateway. In 11 cells the change was pushed within minutes of the p99 jump (23:38–23:52). Disk utilisation went from 41% to 97%, disk read queue wait from 9 to 205 ms, and node-side GET time from 61 to 262 ms. Cell aps-3 got 5.8 but skipped the config push. Its p99 stayed at about 94 ms. Gateways in euw-1 were rolled back on 6 Nov and p99 did not change. A fleet rollback would cost about 4 hours and reopen the signature vulnerability. It would not fix latency. Network and traffic growth don't explain it: round-trip times are normal and GET traffic is up only 6%.

Next steps: revert the compaction change in one cell, for example aps-1 or use-1. Watch GET p99 and backlog, then extend the revert to the other cells. Backlog was 11.2% on 2 Nov, and the on-call projection says it won't reach 15% before 13 Nov. Don't pause compaction, which is unsafe. Hold off on limiting Orrin's ingest until the 10 Nov attribution job shows what is driving backlog growth. Also fix the process gap: fleet config pushes never appear on the change calendar. I'm confident in this diagnosis.
